content.text: {"answer":"The supplied papers do not specifically study a strategy of blocking fake information in external search results by checking how removing a page changes the answer. \n\nThey instead address related issues: how search APIs affect agent decision-making and evidence exposure [1], how systems differ in factual reliability in realistic search settings [2], and how generative engines’ citations depend on what pages their internal searches retrieve [3]. They also show that “one-off” visibility or retrieval evidence can be unreliable across time or runs, implying you may need repeated measurement rather than a single check [4], and that retrieval-time safeguards are important because systems can leak or fabricate when retrieval signals fail [6, 7].","grounded":false}
